scenes.title: 2004 Regensburg 3-Scan Gallery: Launching a 60-Second 3-Ball Cascade Beside the T1-T2-T3 MRI Lightbox
scenes.era: 2004, Department of Neurology, University of Regensburg, Germany

layout.description: Sunlit 2004 German neurology gallery where an adult learner launches three saffron-and-cream juggling balls into a high figure-eight cascade beside a 60-second bench stopwatch and a 3-Scan Longitudinal MRI Lightbox (Scan 1 Flat -> Scan 2 +4% hMT+/V5 Peak -> Scan 3 Idle Drop).

positions.who: Bogdan Draganski and Arne May in tailored white neurology coats over collared shirts
positions.where: standing beside the illuminated 3-Scan MRI Lightbox pointing from the Scan-2 bilateral peak to the Scan-3 idle drop
positions.facing: facing the juggling learner and 3-Scan MRI board

positions.who: Adult beginner-turned-juggler in smart knit pullover and slacks
positions.where: standing center-floor launching three textured juggling balls into a crisp eye-level figure-eight cascade past 60 seconds
positions.facing: facing forward tracking high parabolic ball peaks

props.name: three textured juggling balls and 60-second bench stopwatch
props.period_detail: weighted leather-grain practice balls paired with a large analog-digital 60-second qualification timer
props.physical_behavior: State-A hands hold three balls still at waist height -> State-B hands toss brisk alternating figure-eight arcs above eye level as timer clicks past 60 seconds

props.name: illuminated 3-Scan T1-T2-T3 MRI Comparison Lightbox
props.period_detail: 2004 Regensburg structural VBM display contrasting Baseline, Month-3 Peak (+4%), and Month-6 Idle Washout
props.physical_behavior: State-A researcher switches Scan-2 panel bright -> State-B points brass stylus across to the Scan-3 90-day washout recession

actions.verb_sequence: holds three balls ready at waist height -> launches crisp alternating parabolic throws to eye level for 60 continuous seconds -> sets the balls onto a wooden shelf for the 90-day washout
illuminate Scan-2 bilateral hMT+/V5 expansion -> trace the Scan-3 idle recession

reactions.reaction: grins in surprise learning visual-motion radar — not finger muscles — grew by 4 percent
nod confirming reversible structural plasticity in healthy adults

scenes.wardrobe: 2004 clinical-academic white coats over button-downs; learner in clean crew-neck knitwear and chinos.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ninety days of 3-ball juggling physically expands visual-motion gray matter on MRI — and ninety days on the shelf shrinks it halfway back down.

key_visual.description: a sunlit 2004 Regensburg neurology gallery where an adult volunteer juggles three balls in a figure-eight arc beside neurologists pointing to a 3-Scan T1-T2-T3 MRI lightbox

scenes.title: Eye-Level Parabolic Arc Lab: Tracking Peaks Instead of Palms

layout.description: Clean visuomotor studio where a learner keeps eyes locked straight ahead on the top apex of three crossing ball arcs rather than looking down at the hands.

positions.where: tracking high parabolic ball peaks against a wall grid marking arc apexes
positions.facing: facing the eye-level arc apex grid

props.name: wall-mounted parabolic arc apex grid and three bright balls
props.physical_behavior: State-A ball rises into top apex box -> State-B waiting palm catches falling ball without downward glance

actions.verb_sequence: locks gaze at eye-level arc peaks -> catches balls cleanly at the hips without looking down

reactions.reaction: realizes juggling is high-speed visual geometry rather than finger strength

scenes.wardrobe: Smart-casual collared shirt and rolled sleeves.
scenes.recognition_hook: Skilled jugglers never stare at their palms — they lock onto the top peak of every arc.

scenes.title: 2008 Senior Breakthrough: 62-Year-Old Adults Mastering the 3-Ball Cascade

layout.description: Warm sunlit movement studio where two energetic 62-year-old adults toss clean 3-ball cascades beside an Ages 50–67 MRI plasticity board.

positions.who: Two 62-year-old adult learners in comfortable cardigans and polo shirts
positions.where: practicing smooth 3-ball cascades side-by-side in morning light
positions.facing: facing each other across the sunlit wood floor

props.name: soft weighted practice balls and Ages 50–67 Brain Gain placard
props.physical_behavior: State-A 62-year-old scoops third ball from table -> State-B launches steady 3-ball cascade

actions.verb_sequence: scoop up practice balls -> sustain rhythmic 3-ball cascades with steady poise

reactions.reaction: share a proud smile proving 60-year-old cortex still builds fresh gray matter

scenes.wardrobe: Fine-knit cardigan, polo shirt, tailored casual trousers.
scenes.recognition_hook: Sixty-year-olds who learned 3-ball juggling grew the exact same visual-motion gray matter — plus hippocampal memory boosts.

scenes.era: Modern sunlit morning neighborhood park & pickleball court (Outdoor)

layout.description: Open-air sunlit neighborhood park terrace beside green trees where a 54-year-old adult practices a brisk 10-minute 3-ball cascade and paddle volley to keep visuomotor circuits active.

positions.who: 54-year-old active adult in outdoor athletic zip-top
positions.where: standing on a sunlit park walkway tossing a crisp 3-ball cascade beside a park bench

props.name: three outdoor practice balls and pickleball paddle on park bench
props.physical_behavior: State-A picks up three balls from park bench -> State-B tosses brisk eye-level cascade in morning sunshine

reactions.reaction: catches final ball cleanly with energized morning focus

scenes.wardrobe: Breathable navy quarter-zip, khaki joggers, court sneakers.
scenes.lighting: Crisp golden outdoor morning park sunlight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ten playful minutes of weekly 3D hand-eye practice keeps your brain's newly built branches standing.
